whatThisIs: A NON-REGULATORY depth layer. It reads the size facts the organisation has already declared — revenue band and headcount band — and returns guidance about HOW MUCH programme is proportionate: evidence depth, review cadence, role separation, metrics breadth, third-party coverage, AI governance depth, board-pack density. Nothing more.
whatThisIsNot: It is NOT applicability, and it must never become applicability. A release test held sector, jurisdictions, regulatory scope, AI, OT, data, cloud, vendors and concentration constant and moved only revenue (USD 5m -> USD 50bn) and headcount (1-50 -> 100,000+). The applicability objects came back byte-for-byte identical, and that is CORRECT: size does not create a legal obligation. A Fortune 100 and an SMB with the same declared facts owe the same duties. What differs is how much assurance is proportionate to run against them — and that is advice, not scope.
theRuleThisEncodes: CAC-AP-1 §2.2 says absence asks more, and this layer obeys the same discipline in its own register: an organisation that has declared no size gets `undeclared`, which asks for the FULL depth rather than the smallest. A tool that read a missing revenue figure as 'probably small' would quietly recommend a thin programme to whoever had not got round to filling the form.
neverAutomatic: It never sets or clears a profile flag.
It never appears in the `applicability` block of the CAC-AP-1 payload, and `archetype-advisory.sh` asserts that it does not.
It never touches materiality. The revenue base is a denominator for a human judgement; an archetype is not a threshold and cannot become one.
It never narrows a question set. A skill that skipped a battery because the organisation is small would be inventing an exemption nobody declared.
howTheBandIsChosen: The HIGHER of the two declared bands wins. A 40-person company turning over USD 2bn is not a small organisation, and neither is a 30,000-person company on thin margins. Taking the higher band means a size fact that is unusual for its peer group raises the recommended depth rather than averaging away.

archetypes.title: Size not declared
archetypes.meaning: Neither revenue nor headcount is on record. The full depth is recommended, on the same rule CAC-AP-1 §2.2 applies to a profile flag: absence asks more.
archetypes.evidenceDepth: Ask for the audited artifact or the signed commitment. A questionnaire closes nothing.
archetypes.reviewCadence: Quarterly for critical, annual for the rest, until size is declared.
archetypes.roleSeparation: Assume none is in place and ask who holds each of: risk owner, control owner, approver.
archetypes.thirdPartyCoverage: Every arrangement traced. An untraced dependency is a question, not a low one.
archetypes.whyNotSmallest: A missing revenue figure is not evidence of a small company; it is evidence that nobody filled in the form. Reading it as 'small' would recommend a thin programme to precisely the organisation least likely to notice.

archetypes.title: Small organisation
archetypes.meaning: Under roughly USD 50m or 250 people. Security is usually somebody's second job, and the constraint is attention rather than budget.
archetypes.evidenceDepth: Audited artifact or signed commitment where a requirement must be SATISFIED; elsewhere, record the open question and its date rather than manufacturing assurance.
archetypes.reviewCadence: Annual, with a named trigger for out-of-cycle review.
archetypes.roleSeparation: One person may hold several roles — but the roles are still NAMED, and an approver may not approve their own exception.
archetypes.metricsBreadth: Three to five metrics that would change a decision. A catalogue nobody updates is worse than four numbers somebody defends.
archetypes.thirdPartyCoverage: Trace the arrangements that support a crown jewel. Record the rest as untraced rather than assessing them thinly.
archetypes.aiGovernanceDepth: Inventory everything; run the full battery on deployments that decide or act.
archetypes.boardPackDensity: Short pack. Escalations, decisions, and one figure per section.
archetypes.watchFor: Concentration. A small organisation's single provider is a bigger dependency than a large one's, and the register's criticality trace is the only place that shows.

archetypes.title: Mid-market organisation
archetypes.meaning: Roughly USD 50m–1bn, or 250–5,000 people. Usually the first point at which the programme has to work without the person who built it in the room.
archetypes.evidenceDepth: Tiered evidence enforced. Re-validate an artifact when it ages past its stated period.
archetypes.reviewCadence: Semi-annual overall; quarterly for critical arrangements and deployments.
archetypes.roleSeparation: Risk owner, control owner and approver are three names. The approver is outside the delivery line.
archetypes.metricsBreadth: Eight to fifteen, each with a target and a threshold somebody set on purpose.
archetypes.thirdPartyCoverage: Every arrangement traced or explicitly untraced; exit tested for the critical ones.
archetypes.aiGovernanceDepth: Full battery at `recommends` and above; inventory and exposure derivation for everything.
archetypes.watchFor: The gap between what the register says and what the operating model actually does. This is the band where the two most often diverge.

archetypes.title: Large organisation
archetypes.meaning: Roughly USD 1bn–10bn, or 5,000–50,000 people. Several security functions, several systems of record, and an internal audit function that will read this.
archetypes.evidenceDepth: Tiered, dated, and re-validated on a cadence. An expired artifact escalates rather than lapsing quietly.
archetypes.reviewCadence: Quarterly, with monthly attention review on the operational surface.
archetypes.roleSeparation: Full separation, plus an independent challenge on the criticality assignments themselves.
archetypes.metricsBreadth: Full catalogue, segmented so a group figure cannot hide a division.
archetypes.thirdPartyCoverage: Every arrangement traced, exit tested, subprocessors recorded, concentration measured.
archetypes.aiGovernanceDepth: Full battery on every deployment; shadow-AI discovery run on a cadence, not on report.
archetypes.boardPackDensity: Full pack plus the audit-committee ordering.
archetypes.watchFor: Aggregation hiding a division. A rolled-up figure that cannot be walked back to its source is a figure an audit committee will not accept.

archetypes.title: Enterprise / group
archetypes.meaning: Above roughly USD 10bn, or 50,000 people. Multiple legal entities, multiple perimeters, and the near-certainty that two parts of the group describe the same fact differently.
archetypes.evidenceDepth: Tiered and independently verified. A group assertion is not evidence for a subsidiary.
archetypes.reviewCadence: Quarterly at group, on the subsidiary's own cadence beneath it.
archetypes.roleSeparation: Full separation at every entity, and a named owner for the reconciliation BETWEEN entities.
archetypes.metricsBreadth: Full catalogue with entity segmentation and a stated normalisation method.
archetypes.thirdPartyCoverage: Group-wide, with fourth parties and shared-provider concentration explicit.
archetypes.aiGovernanceDepth: Full battery, per entity, with the group's own declaration never overriding a subsidiary's subject-level fact (CAC-AP-1 §2.3).
archetypes.boardPackDensity: Full pack per entity, plus a group view that names its disagreements rather than resolving them.
archetypes.watchFor: One perimeter presented as the group's. The applicability profile conflict check exists for exactly this, and at this size it fires for real reasons.

revenueBands.note: Read from the banded revenue the store already renders. The exact figure is never used here — an archetype is a coarse judgement and does not need a precise input, and using the exact figure would put it one step from becoming a threshold.

headcountBands.note: Matched loosely against the declared `headcountBand` string, because it is a free declaration rather than an enum — this skill does not own an org-size scale any more than it owns a criticality scale. An unrecognised value contributes NOTHING rather than being coerced, and if it is the only size fact on record the answer is `undeclared`.
